articles.title: Hospital Metropolitano em Campinas: obra de 36 meses é iniciada | G1
articles.standfirst: Com investimento de R$ 436 milhões, unidade terá 400 leitos para atender pacientes do SUS e promete ampliar a oferta de serviços de média e alta complexidade na região.
articles.summary: Com investimento de R$ 436 milhões, unidade terá 400 leitos para atender pacientes do SUS e promete ampliar a oferta de serviços de média e alta complexidade na região.
articles.body:
Projeto do novo Hospital Metropolitano, que será construído em Campinas — Foto: Divulgação/Secretaria Estadual de Saúde

O lançamento da pedra fundamental do Hospital Metropolitano de Campinas , nesta quinta-feira (12), marcou o início oficial das obras da unidade. Participaram do evento o governador Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), e o prefeito da metrópole, Dário Saadi (Republicanos). Com investimento de R$ 436 milhões , o complexo deverá ser entregue em até 36 meses .

A expectativa é que a unidade atue em gargalos históricos na saúde pública de alta e média complexidade na região de Campinas, como filas, atrasos e sobrecargas de exames, internações, consultas e procedimentos .

Do total de 400 leitos previstos, 262 serão destinados à internação e 60 à Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI). O projeto inclui oito salas cirúrgicas, três salas de procedimentos de Hospital Dia, 20 consultórios, 16 poltronas para quimioterapia e 20 para hemodiálise.

O Hospital Estadual de Campinas terá atendimento em áreas como oncologia, neurocirurgia, ortopedia, cardiologia, urologia, cirurgia vascular, cirurgia plástica e psiquiatria.

"Era fundamental abrir esse hospital porque a gente viu em todos os estudos a carência de leitos que nós tínhamos", disse Tarcísio.

Segundo Dário Saadi, a implantação do Hospital Metropolitano atende a uma demanda histórica dos municípios da região.

"A Região Metropolitana identificou, junto com todo o setor de saúde de Campinas, que há uma falta de leitos de média e alta complexidade. O Governo do Estado, através da Tabela SUS Paulista, ampliou o número de leitos aqui na região, mas esses leitos do Hospital Estadual de Campinas são leitos de alta e média complexidade, que é o que temos mais filas na região", afirmou o prefeito.

O governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, e o prefeito de Campinas (SP), Dário Saadi, participam do lançamento da pedra fundamental do Hospital Metropolitano; obra tem previsão de ficar pronta em 36 meses — Foto: Carlos Bassan/PMC

A transferência foi formalizada por decreto estadual publicado em março deste ano, após autorização aprovada pela Câmara Municipal.

A futura unidade estará ao lado de outros equipamentos de saúde que atendem o SUS no município, como o Hospital Municipal Dr. Mário Gatti, a Unidade Pediátrica Mário Gattinho, o Ambulatório Médico de Especialidades (AME) e o Centro de Referência de Diagnóstico em Oncologia (CDO).

A obra está na fase de terraplanagem e segundo a previsão deverá gerar até 408 empregos diretos no pico da construção, além de cerca de 600 postos de trabalho indiretos .

Área doada pela Prefeitura de Campinas (SP) onde será construído o Hospital Metropolitano — Foto: Carlos Bassan/PMC

articles.title: Dieta líquida em Sumaré: pacientes acamados estão sem o alimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Alimento especial é direito garantido pelo SUS e gera custo de R$ 600 mensais às famílias. Município disse que o problema ocorreu por uma falta pontual de determinados tipos de dietas e prevê normalização na próxima semana.
articles.summary: Município disse que o problema ocorreu por uma falta pontual de determinados tipos de dietas e prevê normalização na próxima semana.
articles.body:
Pacientes acamados de Sumaré (SP) estão há pelo menos dois meses sem receber a dieta líquida fornecida pela prefeitura . O alimento especial, que é o único meio de nutrição para pessoas que usam sonda, é um direito garantido pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

A interrupção no fornecimento afeta diretamente a renda das famílias que precisam comprar o produto por conta própria:

Um litro da fórmula custa cerca de R$ 20 ;

O gasto mensal para a alimentação ultrapassa os R$ 600 ;

A distribuição gratuita pelo município é uma obrigação legal regulamentada pela Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa).

Procurada, a Secretaria de Saúde de Sumaré informou que não tem pendências financeiras com as empresas fornecedoras e que o problema ocorreu por uma falta pontual de determinados tipos de dietas por parte delas, o que resultou em entregas parciais .

A pasta afirmou que enviou um ofício às empresas cobrando a entrega imediata dos produtos e que o fornecimento começou a ser regularizado nesta quarta-feira (11). A previsão do município é que todos os itens solicitados sejam entregues até a próxima semana .

Pacientes acamados de Sumaré estão há dois meses sem receber dieta líquida da prefeitura — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A aposentada Maria, de 85 anos, está acamada há mais de dois anos e depende da dieta por sonda nasogástrica. A filha dela, Sueli de Lourdes Francisco, relata o impacto financeiro, já que a mãe recebe apenas um salário mínimo e a família gasta R$ 700 mensais apenas com medicamentos .

"A gente já está há um mês comprando, né? Porque está faltando dieta desde o dia 1º de outubro. Então, a gente que está comprando, fazendo os esforços para poder comprar, para não deixar ela sem o alimento", afirma Sueli de Lourdes Francisco.

A moradora destaca a dificuldade em manter os cuidados básicos diários da mãe idosa.

"Muitas das vezes sobra até para alguém da família, alguns da família, está ajudando, mas está difícil para todo mundo", diz.

articles.title: Conexão Cirúrgica: Hospital Unimed Teresina apresenta avanços a médicos cooperados | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reuniu profissionais para apresentar novos equipamentos, ferramentas digitais e iniciativas voltadas à segurança dos pacientes e à melhoria dos procedimentos cirúrgicos.
articles.summary: Evento reuniu profissionais para apresentar novos equipamentos, ferramentas digitais e iniciativas voltadas à segurança dos pacientes e à melhoria dos procedimentos cirúrgicos.
articles.body:
Conexão Cirúrgica reuniu médicos cooperados no Hospital Unimed Primavera. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

A Unimed Teresina reuniu médicos cooperados, cirurgiões e equipes assistenciais nesta quarta-feira (11), no Hospital de Alta Complexidade Unimed Primavera (HUP), para apresentar as inovações que estão transformando a rotina da unidade hospitalar. O “Conexão Cirúrgica”, promoveu um espaço para a troca de experiências entre os profissionais e a diretoria da cooperativa, fortalecendo o diálogo com quem está diariamente à frente do cuidado clínico e assistencial dos procedimentos cirúrgicos.

Ao longo da programação, os participantes conheceram sete estações temáticas, com demonstrações práticas de equipamentos, ferramentas digitais e processos adotados pelo hospital. Entre as novidades apresentadas estiveram o Dr. Next, que acompanha toda a jornada do paciente no centro cirúrgico; o Projeto Green de Sustentabilidade Hospitalar e o Avvigo, sistema de ultrassom intravascular com recursos de inteligência artificial. Os médicos também tiveram acesso às estratégias de prevenção de infecções hospitalares, aos indicadores de segurança assistencial e aos projetos previstos para 2027.

Os médicos conheceram novos equipamentos, ferramentas digitais e processos do HUP. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

Para os profissionais que participaram do encontro, a oportunidade de conhecer de perto essas melhorias representa um avanço importante na rotina médica. O cirurgião Dr. Fernando Couto de Oliveira destacou especialmente as soluções digitais que facilitam o acompanhamento dos pacientes e a comunicação com as equipes do hospital.

"Tivemos contato com inovações que surpreenderam pelo esforço da equipe em proporcionar melhorias ao cirurgião. Aplicativos e plataformas digitais agora nos permitem acompanhar o status do paciente sem a dependência de processos manuais ou deslocamentos desnecessários, conferindo muito mais agilidade e segurança", pontuou.

A avaliação também foi compartilhada pelo cardiologista intervencionista Dr. Antenor Portela, que ressaltou a estrutura disponível para a realização de procedimentos de alta complexidade. Para ele, iniciativas como o “Conexão Cirúrgica” permitem que os cooperados conheçam melhor os recursos oferecidos pelo hospital e ampliem a integração entre as diferentes especialidades.

"Este evento congrega os médicos e expõe a verdadeira capacidade operacional do HUP. O Hospital Unimed Primavera é a vitrine do grupo cooperativo no Piauí, especialmente na cardiologia intervencionista. Os procedimentos mais complexos e inovadores da região são realizados aqui porque reunimos corpo técnico qualificado, tecnologia avançada e a retaguarda do plano de saúde", afirmou.

Os médicos conheceram soluções digitais que facilitam o acompanhamento da jornada cirúrgica dos pacientes. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

Aproximação com os cooperados e cuidado com os pacientes

Mais do que apresentar novos recursos, o Conexão Cirúrgica foi pensado para ouvir os médicos e fortalecer sua participação no desenvolvimento do hospital. A proposta é que os profissionais conheçam as melhorias realizadas, compartilhem suas necessidades e contribuam para o aperfeiçoamento contínuo dos serviços.

Segundo o presidente da Unimed Teresina, Dr. Rodrigo Oliveira, essa aproximação ganha ainda mais importância no ano em que o Hospital Unimed Primavera completa uma década de operação plena. A unidade possui Acreditação ONA Nível 1, reconhecimento relacionado ao cumprimento de padrões de qualidade e segurança, e trabalha para alcançar o Nível 2, que também avalia a integração dos processos e a gestão hospitalar.

"Este ano o Hospital Unimed Primavera completou 10 anos de operação plena. É um hospital que possui Acreditação ONA Nível 1 e busca a ONA Nível 2, sendo o principal local de trabalho da maioria dos nossos cooperados. O objetivo deste aparato foi convidar os cirurgiões, deixar claro que aqui é a casa deles e mostrar todas as inovações que estamos implantando este ano para facilitar o trabalho e dar segurança à prática médica", declarou.

O vice-presidente da Unimed Teresina, Dr. Rômulo Lages, reforçou que a participação dos cooperados é fundamental para que os investimentos realizados estejam alinhados às necessidades de quem utiliza diariamente a estrutura hospitalar. "O ‘Conexão Cirúrgica’ é essencial para trazer o cirurgião para perto da cooperativa e de sua estrutura. Ele, como dono do negócio, precisa nos dizer o que é realmente importante para que se sinta em casa e escolha a nossa estrutura hospitalar", pontuou.

Essa preocupação também orienta o trabalho das equipes responsáveis pela assistência. Para o coordenador médico do centro cirúrgico, Dr. Tiago Santiago, investir em tecnologia e aprimorar processos só faz sentido quando essas melhorias se refletem na qualidade do atendimento.

"O procedimento cirúrgico é algo complexo, que envolve uma cadeia bastante extensa. Nosso objetivo com este evento é nos aproximar e ficar lado a lado com os profissionais que cuidam dos pacientes. O foco não é simplesmente aumentar o volume cirúrgico, mas cuidar melhor, gerando resultados assistenciais mais sustentáveis", reforçou.

Na mesma linha, o diretor superintendente da Unimed Teresina, Dr. Raimundo Viana, destacou que a estrutura oferecida pelo hospital deve proporcionar confiança aos médicos e tranquilidade aos pacientes e seus familiares.

"Nossa intenção é fazer com que o médico cooperado venha operar no HUP sabendo que ele e seu paciente serão bem acolhidos. Queremos garantir um atendimento cirúrgico seguro, com alta precoce, bem estruturada e excelente resultado clínico", afirmou.

Tecnologia a serviço da precisão e da segurança

Além das inovações tecnológicas, o Conexão Cirúrgica apresentou protocolos de segurança e assistência aos paciente. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

Uma das principais novidades apresentadas no evento foi a plataforma Avvigo, incorporada à estrutura de hemodinâmica do HUP. A tecnologia utiliza ultrassom intravascular, exame que permite visualizar o interior das artérias e obter informações detalhadas sobre suas condições.

Além das novas ferramentas, o hospital apresentou medidas voltadas à segurança em todas as etapas do atendimento cirúrgico. Entre elas estão o acompanhamento de indicadores de infecção, a utilização de protocolos de checagem recomendados pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) e a integração entre as equipes responsáveis pelo cuidado antes, durante e depois das cirurgias.

Ferramentas digitais garantem mais agilidade e segurança na rotina cirúrgica. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

A coordenadora de Enfermagem do Centro Cirúrgico do Hospital Unimed Teresina, Alessandra Oliveira, explicou que essa organização permite acompanhar cada etapa do atendimento, desde a preparação do paciente até sua recuperação.

Conexão Cirúrgica fortaleceu a integração entre médicos e equipes assistenciais. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

"O ‘Conexão Cirúrgica’ permite ao cirurgião compreender os processos desde o pré-operatório até a alta. Essa integração traz benefícios diretos, como a redução dos índices de infecção e a adesão aos checklists da OMS. Mostramos também a retaguarda de suporte intensivo de UTI e o médico prescritor cirúrgico dedicado a acompanhar o paciente no pós-operatório", finalizou.

articles.title: Jovem morre após incêndio em apartamento onde passava férias de SC  | G1
articles.standfirst: Kayto Beller Dias morreu em decorrência de queimaduras. Incêndio em imóvel alugado deixou outros dois feridos.
articles.summary: Kayto Beller Dias morreu em decorrência de queimaduras. Incêndio em imóvel alugado deixou outros dois feridos.
articles.body:
Kayto Beller Dias, natural de Joinville, morreu na quarta-feira (11) — Foto: Redes sociais/Reprodução

Kayto Beller Dias , de 25 anos, morreu nove dias após ficar ferido em um incêndio dentro de um apartamento onde passava férias em São José , na Grande Florianópolis.

O jovem estava hospedado com dois amigos quando o fogo atingiu o apartamento na manhã de domingo, 1° de novembro. O imóvel era alugado por meio de uma plataforma de hospedagens.

Natural de Joinville , no Norte de Santa Catarina , Kayto morreu em decorrência de queimaduras . A morte foi confirmada pela família na manhã de quarta-feira (11). O sepultamento ocorreu nesta quinta (12).

Em conversa com o g1 , um familiar, que preferiu não se identificar, descreveu o jovem como uma pessoa alegre, trabalhadora e muito querida por quem convivia com ele.

"Um menino muito amado por todos, alegre, feliz da vida, trabalhador, sem maldade. Menino de ouro", relatou.

Kayto era formado em administração desde 2024 e estava fazendo uma pós-graduação. A Faculdade INESA, onde ele estudou, publicou uma homenagem ao ex-aluno e manifestou pesar pela morte.

"Neste momento de tristeza, expressamos nossa solidariedade aos familiares, amigos, colegas e professores, desejando força e conforto diante desta perda".

O incêndio aconteceu por volta das 5h50 em um apartamento no nono andar de um edifício residencial na Rua Elizeu Di Bernardi, no bairro Campinas,.

Segundo os bombeiros, quando as equipes chegaram ao local, as chamas haviam sido controladas pelos próprios moradores e pelo síndico, que utilizaram o sistema hidráulico preventivo do condomínio.

Três pessoas ficaram feridas na ocorrência e receberam atendimento médico. Um homem de 33 anos apresentava queimaduras de primeiro e segundo graus, além de ter inalado fumaça. Ele estava consciente e orientado e foi encaminhado ao Hospital Regional de São José.

As outras duas vítimas também foram atendidas e transportadas para avaliação médica com ferimentos de menor gravidade.

articles.title: Acidente na AM-010: passageiro morre após táxi capotar e incendiar | G1
articles.standfirst: Outras três pessoas ficaram feridas no acidente e foram levadas ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro Dr. João Lúcio. O estado de saúde delas não foi divulgado.
articles.summary: O acidente na AM-010 ocorreu nesta quinta (12) e deixou três feridos levados ao Hospital João Lúcio após o táxi capotar e pegar fogo na Zona Norte de Manaus.
articles.body:
Carro foi totalmente consumido pelas chamas — Foto: Divulgação

Antônio Lima de Silva de 40 anos morreu após o táxi em que estava capotar e pegar fogo na manhã desta quinta-feira (12), na rodovia AM-010, na Zona Norte de Manaus . Outras três pessoas ficaram feridas.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), o acidente ocorreu entre os quilômetros 32 e 33 da rodovia, nas proximidades do bairro Lago Azul. A corporação foi acionada por volta das 5h.

Quando chegaram ao local, os bombeiros encontraram o veículo capotado e em chamas. Antônio Lima ficou preso sob o carro e teve a morte confirmada no local por uma equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

Além de Antônio, estavam no táxi o motorista, de 34 anos, e outros dois passageiros. Os três feridos receberam atendimento do Samu, com apoio da equipe de resgate dos bombeiros, e foram levados para o Hospital e Pronto-Socorro Dr. João Lúcio, na Zona Leste da capital. O estado de saúde deles não foi divulgado.

De acordo com a Polícia Militar, quando a equipe chegou ao local, o incêndio já havia sido controlado pelos bombeiros e os sobreviventes recebiam os primeiros socorros.

A área foi isolada para o trabalho do Departamento de Polícia Técnico-Científica (DPTC) e da Delegacia Especializada em Homicídios e Sequestros (DEHS).

O corpo de Antônio Lima de Silva foi removido pelo Instituto Médico Legal (IML). Os familiares foram orientados a registrar o caso em uma delegacia para que as causas do acidente sejam investigadas.

articles.title: Top 4 Prostate Cancer Symptoms a Doctor Monitors in Himself As New Guidelines Urge Regular Screening
articles.summary: Prostate cancer symptoms a Mayo Clinic doctor monitors in his own body include urination changes and blood in the urine. New PSA screening guidelines released.
articles.body: Prostate cancer has been called an “epidemic of the modern age.” One in eight men will be diagnosed during their lifetime, and though most of them won’t die from it, prostate cancer remains the second-leading cause of cancer death in men, after lung cancer. Now, the American Cancer Society is urging regular screening, a key change from previous recommendations, which advised men only to talk with their doctor about whether testing makes sense. But the updated guidelines, published on Thursday, Nov. 12, instruct men who are between 50 and 69 years old and have an average risk of developing prostate cancer to be screened every two years. Patients at high risk, including Black men and those with a strong family history of prostate cancer, should undergo annual screenings beginning at age 45. NBC News medical contributor Dr. Akshay Syal called it a “pretty significant shift” — the first guideline change in more than 16 years. The message to men is: “You should get screened,” he noted. “The hope is to catch these things earlier,” Syal said on TODAY. Black men have a 67% higher incidence of the disease and almost double the mortality rate compared to white men, “an inequity that needs immediate reversal,” said Dr. William Dahut, chief scientific officer at the American Cancer Society, in a statement. The first step in screening is done with a blood test that measures the level of prostate-specific antigen (PSA), a protein made by the prostate. Abnormally high PSA levels may indicate a tumor, but secondary testing such as an MRI can determine who needs a biopsy and help avoid aggressive treatment of prostate cancers that aren’t life-threatening, the guidelines note. “PSA testing remains the cornerstone of detecting prostate cancer early, and we now have stronger evidence of its benefits,” said Dr. Robert Smith, director of the Center for Early Cancer Detection at the American Cancer Society, in a statement. When it comes to older men, the balance of benefits and harms remains “uncertain,” so those who are 70 to 74 years old should make a decision with their doctor on whether to be screened, the new guidelines note. Screening is not recommended for men who are 75 or older. ‘Take It Seriously’ The widespread impact of the disease is one reason Dr. Dan Childs became interested in treating it. “What stuck out to me was how common prostate cancer is. Prostate cancer is one of those diseases that’s so common that almost every family’s been touched by it,” Childs, a medical oncologist at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, who specializes in treating patients with genitourinary cancers, tells TODAY.com. “I want men to take a diagnosis of prostate cancer seriously.” It’s estimated there will be more than 333,000 new cases in the U.S. in 2026, and 36,320 men will die from the disease. Former President Joe Biden is a high-profile patient. TODAY’s Al Roker was also treated for the disease. Older age is a risk factor. The chance of having prostate cancer “rises rapidly” after 50, the American Cancer Society notes. By the time men reach 70, almost half (46%), have some cancer cells in their prostate, a study found. ‘Silent Disease’ Doctors don’t know why the chestnut-sized gland — located just below the bladder and part of the male reproductive system — is so vulnerable to cancer, Childs says. Many men are surprised to learn prostate cancer is usually found through routine screening — not because it sends warning signs, he notes. It’s a “silent disease,” especially in the curable stages, researchers note. “Don’t wait for symptoms,” Childs warns. “Early prostate cancer can have no symptoms at all. So if you’re in your 40s or your 50s, especially if you have a family history of prostate cancer, it’s time to start talking with your doctor about whether PSA screening might be right for you.” As Childs treats men with prostate cancer, the possibility of developing the disease himself is on his mind as well. Knowing what he knows, here are the prostate cancer warning signs the doctor would pay attention to in his own body. He emphasizes most men don’t have symptoms. Persistent Changes in Urination This includes having a weak urinary stream, difficulty starting urination or waking up at night more often to go to the bathroom than before, Childs says. It could happen because an enlarged prostate can cause a mechanical obstruction as urine is leaving the body, and make it tougher to push the urine past it, he notes. “I’d pay particular attention to those types of symptoms,” Childs says, calling them the most common warning signs if symptoms do appear. Blood in the Urine This may happen if the cancer is causing irritation in the lining along the path of the urine. “You have to be particularly vigilant when you’re seeing blood in a location that it shouldn’t be. That’s something never to ignore,” the doctor cautions. “So if you’re seeing blood in your urine, pay attention to that.” New Bone Pain Prostate cancer has a proclivity for spreading to bone, so if there’s new pain in the back, hips or pelvis that’s otherwise unexplained and persistent, it’s reason to talk to your doctor, Childs says. He calls this the second most common symptom. Former President Joe Biden is living with a “very debilitating” and “painful” aggressive form of prostate cancer that has metastasized to his bones, his son Hunter Biden recently said. Unexplained Weight Loss Men with more advanced prostate cancer may start to get signals that something’s off, such as losing weight without trying or experiencing persistent fatigue they’ve never felt before, Childs notes. “Those are two symptoms that I take seriously and can occur regardless of somebody’s cancer type,” he says. Prostate Cancer Screening Screening mainly involves a blood test that measures PSA, a protein that’s made by both normal prostate cells and prostate cancer cells, Childs says. Higher levels can be associated with prostate cancer. Based on the initial value of the PSA test and other risk factors, a primary care doctor can help determine when to repeat the testing, Childs notes. It’s key to know whether the disease runs in your family. The digital rectal exam doesn’t have as important of a role as the blood marker, he adds. “I don’t want the fear of a digital rectal exam to be a reason that men don’t seek prostate cancer screening because it can be accomplished without a digital rectal exam,” the doctor says. If a man has elevated PSA, he may get an MRI, a biopsy and, in some circumstances, a PET scan. Prostate Cancer Treatment Not all cancers within the prostate are the same — the risk a tumor poses depends on the genetics of the cancer, and what drives it, Childs explains. After a man is diagnosed with prostate cancer, the next step is to figure out whether it’s simply present, or if it could metastasize and cause harm. Doctors work with patients to decide if the cancer needs treatment or not. A low-risk, small, slow-growing tumor can lead to active surveillance with repeat PSA tests, scans and potentially biopsies to make sure it’s “not evolving in a sinister way,” Childs says. More worrisome tumors may require surgery to remove the prostate and radiation. Cancer that has spread to bones usually requires systemic treatments “that go everywhere that blood goes,” such as hormone therapy, intravenous forms of radiation called radiopharmaceuticals and chemotherapy, he notes. “Prostate cancer is impactful, it is common, it’s scary. But our expectation — even if you are diagnosed with prostate cancer — is for you to live many, many years. We will cure a high proportion of men,” Childs says. “In a man diagnosed with advanced prostate cancer, I’ll tell them we’ll always be watching this cancer like a hawk. ... Thankfully, now men with even metastatic or advanced prostate cancer can live more than five to 10 years after diagnosis.” TODAY’s Symptom Check series features doctors, specialists and health experts who reveal the warning signs they’d look for in their own body when it comes to cancer and other diseases.

articles.title: Kota hosp reports new maternal death linked to C-section complications
articles.summary: Kota reports new maternal death after C-section; 36-year-old died from severe lung and kidney infections and multi-organ failure after surgery at JK Lon Hospital.
articles.body: Kota: A fresh death linked to post-caesarean complications in govt hospitals in Kota has renewed concerns after a 36-year-old woman died late Thursday while undergoing treatment for severe lung and kidney infections with urine blockage. Infections following C-sections have claimed at least five mothers in May and four in Oct in govt hospitals in the city.The woman, identified as Priti, underwent a caesarean delivery at JK Lon Hospital on Nov 8 and was shifted to MBS Hospital on Nov 10 as her condition deteriorated. Doctors said she developed critical multi-organ complications and was recommended for transfer to the super speciality block of New Medical College Hospital (NMCH) Thursday, but she died before the transfer could take place.Priti’s husband, Bhanwarlal, had initially taken her to Indergarh Hospital in Bundi for delivery on Diwali (Nov 8), from where she was referred to JK Lon Hospital in Kota the same day. She delivered a baby girl through a C-section, but relatives said her condition worsened soon after surgery.“Patient Priti, carrying a full-term pregnancy with a history of one previous caesarean section, was admitted to JK Lon Hospital on the afternoon of Nov 8 for labour pains,” JK Lon Hospital Superintendent Dr Nirmala Sharma said. “Upon admission, her blood pressure was recorded at a high of 160/100 mmHg.” She added that the patient had received antenatal check-ups at Indergarh, Itawa and Sawai Madhopur, and that there was no earlier documentation of high blood pressure during those visits.According to the hospital, investigations on Nov 9 showed rapidly worsening liver parameters. “Her bilirubin levels surged rapidly from 1 to 9, and further up to 11 by the evening, accompanied by deep jaundice,” Dr Sharma said. She said Priti was moved to MBS Hospital on Nov 10 due to multi-organ involvement.At MBS Hospital, treating physician Dr Deepti Sharma confirmed the death. “She remained in a highly critical condition with progressive multi-organ dysfunction affecting both her liver and renal functions,” Dr Sharma said, adding that Priti died late Thursday evening during treatment.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Resident doc found dead in Jodhpur hostel
articles.summary: Female resident doctor Nikki Chaudhary found dead in Umaid Hospital hostel, Jodhpur; police probe underway, cause unknown; UDF seeks independent inquiry.
articles.body: Jodhpur/Jaipur: A female resident doctor was found dead in her hostel room under suspicious circumstances at Umaid Hospital in Jodhpur Thursday.The deceased, identified as Nikki Chaudhary, was found unconscious inside her room and was rushed to the trauma centre of MDM Hospital, where doctors declared her dead at around 6 pm.Chaudhary, a native of Jhunjhunu, was a first-year postgraduate student of the 2025 batch in the anaesthesia department. She was staying in room number 312 of the PG hostel at Umaid Hospital.MDM Hospital superintendent Vikas Rajpurohit said Nikki had been unwell since Wednesday and was suffering from vomiting and diarrhoea. Due to her illness, she had taken leave Wednesday.She had reportedly remained in her hostel room since Thursday morning.According to preliminary information, when her fellow residents knocked on her room’s door in the evening and received no response, they alerted the hospital management. She was subsequently found unconscious and taken to MDM Hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead.The hostel room has been sealed, and police have initiated an investigation to ascertain the circumstances surrounding her death. The exact cause of death is yet to be established.Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), a doctors’ organisation, has urged the National Medical Commission and Rajasthan Medical Education Department to ensure an independent, time-bound investigation in the alleged resident doctor suicide case in Jodhpur medical college. He said, “A medical degree should never come at the cost of a young doctor’s dignity, safety or mental well-being. articles.title: Forest tracker falls from vehicle in Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve, dies
articles.summary: Volunteer tiger tracker Kamal Bairwa, 42, died after falling from a moving forest department camper in Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve; driver booked for negligence.
articles.body: Kota: A 42-year-old volunteer tiger tracker in Bundi’s Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve died Wednesday after he fell from a moving forest department vehicle inside the reserve.The deceased was identified as Kamal Bairwa, son of Ramnath Bairwa, a resident of Devpura village under Dei police station in Bundi district.Police handed over the body to the family after a post-mortem at MBS Hospital mortuary in Kota Thursday morning. On the basis of a report by family members, Dei police registered a case of negligent driving against the driver of the forest camper vehicle, also a volunteer tracker.Deputy Conservator of Forest Arun Kumar D said Bairwa was part of a team of officials ferrying beds and cots for volunteers at an internal sanctuary watchtower so they could rest after completing tracking activities. The forest department sent in a camper vehicle loaded with the materials, with one volunteer -- Bairwa -- seated in the rear, another driving the vehicle, and a department staffer following the vehicle on a two-wheeler.“As the vehicle approached within 500 metres of the gate, the driver noticed that the volunteer seated in the back had fallen off,” DCF Arun Kumar said.Kumar said when staff rushed back to check on Bairwa, he reportedly said he had felt sudden dizziness before losing consciousness. The fall led to severe head injuries and heavy bleeding.Bairwa was first taken to Bundi for preliminary treatment and later referred to Kota for advanced care. He died during treatment at a private hospital despite efforts to resuscitate him, the DCF said.The forest department is coordinating financial support for the family and exploring govt assistance schemes, including eligibility under Ayushman Bharat, he added.Dei police station SHO Hanuman Sahay said a case of negligent driving was lodged against the driver after the family alleged negligence. articles.title: Row over childlessness, drinking ends in man’s murder in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru loan agent Rajashekhar, 43, allegedly stabbed dead by wife Malashri, 35, after a quarrel over childlessness and his drinking habit.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A 43-year-old private bank loan agent was allegedly stabbed to death by his wife during a domestic quarrel at their Lakshmipura home in south Bengaluru Wednesday night.The deceased, Rajashekhar, was allegedly stabbed in the chest-abdomen region with a kitchen knife by Malashri, 35, around 10.30pm. He sustained severe injuries and died on the spot.Preliminary investigation indicated that the couple frequently quarrelled over not having children and Rajashekhar’s alleged drinking habit. On Wednesday night, Rajashekhar is said to have returned home drunk and blamed Malashri for their childlessness, following which the argument escalated and she allegedly stabbed him.Neighbours became suspicious after hearing the couple quarrelling before a sudden silence. They entered the house and found Rajashekhar lying in a pool of blood. They alerted police and took him to Victoria Hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.The couple had married five years ago and lived on the first floor of a residential building owned by Rajashekhar’s family. His parents occupied the ground floor. Rajashekhar worked as a loan agent, helping loan applicants with documentation and submitting applications to banks.During questioning, Malashri confessed to stabbing her husband after losing control. articles.title: Brother-in-law stabs Kota jeweller to death over family dispute
articles.summary: Kota jeweller Maulik Jain, 39, was stabbed to death by his brother-in-law outside a Dadabari hospital after a family dispute; accused detained.
articles.body: Kota: A 39-year-old jeweller was stabbed to death by his brother-in-law outside the intensive care unit of a trust-run hospital in Dadabari police station area Thursday morning. Police detained the accused and filed charges under relevant sections.The victim, Maulik Jain (39), lived in Talwandi and was a jeweller. Maulik and his wife had gone to the hospital to check on his mother-in-law, who was admitted there for a head injury sustained when she fell off a motorcycle near the Kota Barrage culvert Wednesday night.During their hospital visit around 10:30 am, Maulik and his brother-in-law, Kapil Jain, an artificial jewellery shop owner, had an argument over a family matter.According to Dadabari police station circle inspector Baldev Ram, the verbal altercation quickly escalated when Kapil whipped out a knife and stabbed his brother-in-law in the chest.The victim was first treated within the hospital before being referred to Kota Heart Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The body was shifted to the medical college hospital.The incident prompted the local business community to shut their shops in Sarafa Bazaar as a mark of protest.Family members said that the two brothers-in-law had disputes earlier too, but they were resolved through mediation. According to police, initial findings point to an ongoing family feud as the motive. articles.title: Mom, 3 kids burnt alive as fire engulfs 19 houses in Arunachal
articles.summary: Fire in Arunachal’s Parsi-Parlo killed a mother and 3 children, destroyed 19 kutcha houses; blaze likely started in a kitchen; relief camp set up.
articles.body: Guwahati: A woman and her three children were burnt alive in their sleep after a fire swept through the densely populated Parsi-Parlo township in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey district early Thursday, completely destroying 19 kutcha houses and partially damaging five structures.The fire broke out around 1am and quickly spread from one house to another. The deceased were identified as Dongda Yanu, in her 30s, and her three children — sons Dongda Karsang and Dongda Maji, and daughter Dongda Amji. All four were asleep when the fire engulfed the house, locals said. Their charred bodies were difficult to identify, officials said.Yanu’s husband, Dongda Taji, suffered serious burn injuries and was taken to a hospital in Itanagar.“Preliminary investigations suggest that the fire originated in a local kitchen before spreading to neighbouring houses,” a district official said.The township, located between the Parsi and Parlo rivers, has a densely packed settlement, allowing the flames to spread rapidly. Authorities have appealed to residents to decongest the area and relocate to nearby locations.“The town is very compact and the population is concentrated in one area. So fire quickly engulfed the area,” the official said.The township’s difficult terrain and poor road connectivity hampered the emergency response. The nearest fire station and emergency services station are at Koloriang, the district headquarters, around 45 km away. By the time fire and emergency officials reached the area around 10am — nearly nine hours after the blaze began — the houses had been reduced to ashes.“Since everything was already finished by morning, the fire tenders did not arrive. Only officials came for assessment,” a district official said.Additional deputy commissioner Nabam Tajik said residents barely had time to save their belongings as the fire spread while they were asleep. “People could not collect any item as they just woke up from deep sleep and ran for safety. The damage will be in crores,” he said.The District Disaster Management Authority has set up a relief camp at the Government Secondary School in Parsi-Parlo, where 23 people from three families are taking shelter. Another 16 families have moved into the homes of relatives in the township.CM Pema Khandu expressed grief over the tragedy and said the incident had left several families homeless.“The reports of loss of lives and missing family members make this tragedy even more heartbreaking. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. I pray for strength and courage for everyone affected by this unfortunate incident,” Khandu wrote in a social media post.The latest tragedy comes months after Parsi-Parlo, a remote border township located in difficult hilly terrain, suffered widespread devastation from flash floods triggered by continuous monsoon rain.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Woman stabbed by friend for ending relationship in Chennai
articles.summary: Woman, 32, critically injured after friend stabbed her for ending relationship near Mangadu, Chennai; suspect Sampath, 38, arrested by police.
articles.body: Chennai: A 32-year-old woman was critically injured after a man stabbed her in the chest for ending their relationship near Mangadu on Thursday morning. Police arrested the suspect.Police said the victim, Kasthuri of Periya Koluthuvanchery near Paraniputhur, had been living with her children after separating from her husband. She and Sampath, 38, a tile worker from the same locality, became friends a few months ago.However, over the past few weeks, Kasthuri had been avoiding Sampath and eventually ended the relationship. Angered by her decision, Sampath entered her house early Thursday and confronted her. He then stabbed Kasthuri before fleeing. Hearing her screams, neighbours rushed to her rescue and took her to a govt hospital. Her condition is said to be critical.
